newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn sees no Euro without France.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn sees no Euro without France.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Tuesday that there cannot be European monetary union without France.
"I do not believe the euro can come about without France," Strauss-Kahn told RTL radio.
Strauss-Kahn also repeated that France was committed to meeting the timetable for the launch of the single European currency.
"We want to do the euro and we want to do it at the scheduled date of January 1, 1999," he said.
"If France did not join, who would be left Germany, Denmark?," he added.
He said that European monetary union would help France and Europe's drive to boost employment.
"When the euro will come about it will serve employment," he said.
